claims.text: The baseline is an as-cast equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr alloy has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr alloy has an elevated-temperature yield strength of approximately 855 MPa.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr alloy has a density of approximately 10.2 g/cm3.
The proposed intervention is to substitute Al for part of the Hf in HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed modified composition is Hf0.85Al0.15MoTaTiZr.
The intervention introduces roughly 15 atomic percent Al in place of Hf.
Al is much lighter than Hf.
Replacing part of the Hf with Al will reduce the alloy's density.
Al can dissolve into a single-phase BCC matrix in the proposed Hf-Al-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr composition.
The modified alloy will remain a single-phase BCC solid solution with lattice distortion and microstructural homogeneity similar to the baseline.
Dissolved Al will provide solid-solution strengthening through lattice distortion.
Maintaining the transition between screw and edge dislocation mechanisms will preserve high yield strength and ductility at room and elevated temperatures.
The modified alloy will have an 8-15% lower density than the as-cast baseline.
The modified alloy's room-temperature and 1000°C yield strengths and ductility will remain within approximately 10% of the baseline values.
The density reduction combined with retained mechanical properties will improve specific strength.
Prior MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW alloys had BCC structures, approximately 400 MPa yield strength at 1600°C, high density, and very low room-temperature compressive ductility.
Other refractory high-entropy alloys can retain substantial strength over broad elevated-temperature ranges.

contradictions.description: Hf0.85Al0.15MoTaTiZr normalizes to approximately Hf17Al3Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 at.%, so it contains about 3 at.% Al, not the roughly 15 at.% Al stated in the intervention text. A literal 15 at.% replacement of Hf in equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr would instead give approximately Hf5Al15Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20.

The prediction specifies an 8-15% density reduction, but the rejection rule only falsifies the hypothesis below 5%; therefore, a 5-8% reduction would miss the stated prediction without triggering rejection.
